'''Tiberiu Popoviciu''' (February 16, 1906–October 29, 1975) was a [[Romania]]n mathematician<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.cs.ubbcluj.ro/profesor-tiberiu-popoviciu/|title=Profesor Tiberiu Popoviciu|first=Wolfgang|last=Breckner|publisher=[[Babeș-Bolyai University]], Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics|accessdate=2015-04-19}}.</ref> and the namesake of [[Popoviciu's inequality]] and [[Popoviciu's inequality on variances]].

The [[Tiberiu Popoviciu High School of Computer Science]] in [[Cluj-Napoca]] is named after him.<ref>[http://www.li.cj.edu.ro/index.php/despre-noi/istoric Istoric], [[Tiberiu Popoviciu High School of Computer Science]] (in Romanian), retrieved 2015-04-19.</ref>

In 1951 he founded a research institute which now bears his name: [[Tiberiu Popoviciu Institute of Numerical Analysis]].

==Biography==

Popoviciu was born in [[Arad, Romania|Arad]] in 1906, and attended high school in his hometown, the school which is now the [[Moise Nicoară National College]]. He graduated from the [[University of Bucharest]], and got his doctorate in 1933 under [[Paul Montel]] from [[Paris-Sorbonne University]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|40735}}</ref>

He was a lecturer at the Universities of [[Chernivtsi University|Cernăuți]], [[University of Bucharest|Bucharest]], and [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University|Iași]]. In 1946 he was appointed professor at the [[Babeș-Bolyai University|University of Cluj]]. On June 4, 1937 Popoviciu was elected a corresponding member of the [[Romanian Academy of Sciences]]. In November 1948 he was elected a corresponding member of the [[Romanian Academy]]. He became full member of the mathematical sciences section of the Academy on March 20, 1963.

He married his former student, [[Elena Moldovan Popoviciu]], in 1964; she also became a notable functional analyst.<ref>{{MacTutor|id=Popoviciu_Elena|title=Elena Moldovan Popoviciu}}</ref> He died in 1975 in Cluj-Napoca, and is buried in the city's [[Hajongard cemetery|Hajongard Cemetery]].
